title: Ridgecrest decay estimates rise when fits from day 1 end at day 30 instead of day 14 in a 100 km USGS sample
abstract: We tested how the time window and magnitude threshold affect power-law decay estimates for the 2019 Ridgecrest sequence. We used a fixed USGS catalog snapshot within 100 km of the M7.1 event. For events with magnitude at least 2.5 and a fit start at day 1, the decay exponent increased from 0.844 for days 1-14 to 1.006 for days 1-30. The paired increase was 0.162. Its daily block multiplier interval was 0.089 to 0.295, and its three-day block interval was 0.059 to 0.363. The increase at magnitude at least 3.0 also kept a positive three-day interval. The interval at magnitude at least 3.5 included zero. Radius changes from 100 km to 50 km had a smaller effect on the day 1-30 estimates. A threshold difference from fits that start at hour 1 became uncertain when fits started at day 1. These are descriptive estimates from one sequence. The block intervals depend on assumptions about time dependence. The study cannot separate detection loss, changes in magnitude distribution, secondary triggering, and model error. The package contains the source snapshot, derived data, code, figures, and independent numerical checks.
